requirements.requirement: Nginx on node1 serves a successful HTTP response for `/` on TCP port 6500.
requirements.summary: Before and after the mandatory restart, Nginx was active and listening on IPv4 and IPv6 port 6500. Requests to node1's managed address returned HTTP 200 with page content. The changed boot identity and recovered response also demonstrate persistence.

overall_summary: The task outcome is satisfied. Direct checks showed HTTP 200 at `/` on TCP 6500 both before and after a bounded node restart. The restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, observed disruption, different post-restart boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service and page content. Hygiene was strong apart from the retained, unnecessary default port-80 listeners.
limitations: The HTTP requests originated on node1 using its managed IP, so off-host network traversal was not independently tested.
The captured firewall evidence verifies port 6500 but does not establish whether the additional port-80 listener was reachable through firewalld.

operational_hygiene.summary: All deliberate state-changing actions had clear task or mandatory restart-protocol roles, and no abandoned troubleshooting mutations were found. The only unnecessary retained effect was activation of Nginx's package-default all-interface port-80 listeners during installation and service startup; these remained in the final socket snapshot despite not supporting the requested port-6500 outcome. Evidence does not establish whether firewalld admitted inbound traffic on port 80, limiting the severity. No failed services, abnormal temporary residue, or package inconsistency was observed.
